newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude steady as physical barrels move.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude steady as physical barrels move.

text.p: Brent crude was marginally firmer, judging by the last physical deal at December Brent -36 cents for a second decade loader but North Sea differentials were generally depressed with demand for sweet barrels weak.

An earlier Brent deal for a Nov 8-10 loader at Dec Brent -50 cents was not seen indicative of the market, with the seller having picked up the cargo a day earlier in anticipation of longer operational problems at the Heidrun field, a trader said.

One of Friday's Brent dates, a Nov 17-19 loader was later sold at December Brent -36 cents, some four cents up on Thursday's deal. Persistent weakness of Brent appeared to have triggered some buying although most North Sea differentials struggled to achieve a premium to Dated Brent.
A prompt Statfjord cargo was sold at Dated Brent +5 cents, seen by traders as a good number considering other grades like Forties fetched no better than Dated Brent +2 cents at the last trade.

There were unconfirmed reports that two cargoes of Oseberg were sold but no numbers were heard. A Gullfaks A loading November 20-22 was sold at Dated Brent +10 cents and a Fulmar for November 9 fetched Dated Brent +50 cents.
In the paper market, values were notionally higher in afternoon business and paper spreads held steady.

Jan 15-day Brent traded at $23.35 a barrel in the London afternoon, in line with screen levels. The Dec/Jan spread helds its 37-cent backwardation, while the prompt to Dated spread remained in a 35-40 cent contango.

CFD business was active with next week's dates done at Jan +10 cents, some eight cents below Thursday levels. A roll of Nov 12-15 into Nov 18-22 was done at -2 cents and a Nov 18-Dec 13 CFD traded twice at Jan +9 cents.
One trader said the fact that the CFD backwardation curve had come in pointed to perceptions of a weaker market.
